DTC codes C1145 and P1782 are not the typical codes associated with this failure; transfer case chain wear is primarily a mechanical issue diagnosed by noise rather than specific DTCs
Upper cost range ($3500) is low - dealer full transfer case replacement commonly quoted at $5000-$6300; chain-only repair at indie shops can be under $1000
Severity arguably should be higher - sources warn complete failure can lock up drivetrain causing sudden power loss, which is a safety concern
audit.evidence: Multiple sources (MBWorld, Go-Parts, RepairPal, Engine Patrol) confirm the 2007-2016 GL-Class (X164/X166) has a well-documented stretched internal Morse chain issue causing skipping/clicking noise on acceleration, plus secondary bearing whine. However, the GL 4MATIC uses a fixed 50:50 mechanical split without a torque-distribution actuator, contradicting part of the description, and dealer replacement costs commonly reach $5000-$6000.

issues_found: Description conflates differential pinion/axle seals with the more common G-Class swivel ball/wipe seal leaks (king-pin housing)
Brake contamination claim is not well-documented as a typical symptom; leaking grease/oil typically exits through swipe seals onto chromed ball, not brake pads
Repair cost range ($600-$1500) appears low; dealer quotes for proper front axle overhaul commonly run $3000+
Severity 'high' may be overstated - typically classified as a maintenance/wear issue rather than safety-critical unless severely neglected
Year range is reasonable for W463 (1990-2018) but the issue affects the entire W463 production run, not just 2000-2018
audit.evidence: Multiple G-Wagen forums (MBWorld, BenzWorld, ClubGWagen) confirm front axle leaks are a very common W463 issue, but the typical problem is differential oil migrating into the steering knuckle/swivel ball housing and weeping out through wipe seals, requiring a front axle overhaul kit - not a simple differential seal replacement. Real-world repair quotes (e.g., $3500 dealer estimate for a 2017 G63) suggest the listed cost range is underestimated for a proper repair.

Multiple W177 A-Class owner forum threads confirm a clunking/knocking noise from the front suspension traced to top strut mount bearings, with Mercedes having released a modified top bearing and reportedly working through multiple superseded part revisions. No DTCs are typically associated, severity as a nuisance noise is appropriate, and the cost range is reasonable for strut mount or strut replacement.

issues_found: Repair cost upper bound ($1500) is likely overstated — most fixes are free OTA/dealer software updates covered under recall 21V-297/21V-354 or warranty; out-of-warranty head-unit replacement could exceed $1500 but typical repair is $0
Severity 'low' is defensible as nuisance, but note NHTSA recall 21V-297 classified a related MBUX startup/rearview-camera failure as a safety issue — some owners argue it borders on medium
Year range 2020-2025 is broadly accurate for GLB (launched MY2020 with NTG6 MBUX), though the major documented recall covers MY2019-2021 specifically
audit.evidence: NHTSA Recall 21V-297 (Mercedes Campaign 2021080009) affected 342,000+ vehicles including the GLB for MBUX not starting correctly, and Recall 21V-354 addressed MBUX software updates on MY19-21 vehicles including GLA/GLB-class. Owner forums (MBWorld, BenzWorld) document MBUX freezes, screen blackouts, reboots, and CarPlay/Android Auto disconnect issues, typically resolved by dealer software updates at no cost.

issues_found: Year range 2016-2022 spans two distinct GLE generations (W166: 2016-2019 and W167: 2020-2022); most documented differential leak complaints are on the W166 platform, less evidence specifically for W167 (2020-2022)
GLE53 AMG didn't exist until 2021; earlier AMG variants on W166 were GLE43 and GLE63, not GLE53

Repair cost range plausible but may be optimistic — pinion seal replacement on Mercedes typically runs $350-$500+ at independents and higher at dealers; complete diff replacement (if damage occurs) is $2,000-$3,800+
audit.evidence: Differential leaks and failures are documented on W164/W166 Mercedes SUV chassis (including 2016-2019 GLE350/450/GLE43/GLE63), with whining noise as the classic symptom and pinion/axle seal as common leak points. RepairPal estimates pinion seal replacement at $353-$481 average, consistent with the stated range, though dealer quotes and full diff replacements run much higher.

issues_found: Severity likely undercalibrated - multiple sources document vehicles stalling on highways and no-start conditions requiring tows, plus NHTSA recalls for fire risk from loose 48V grounds on related models, suggesting 'high' rather than 'medium'
DTC code P0A7F is a generic OBD-II hybrid battery code; Mercedes-specific 48V faults more commonly report codes like U10F3, P1AFA, U11C3, or internal ECU codes (e.g., 061B00) per technician sources
S-Class specifically has fewer reported cases than E/GLE/GLS/CLS - issue is documented but lower-volume on S-Class
audit.evidence: Multiple owner forums (MBWorld, BenzWorld), a class-action lawsuit filing, and repair guides confirm widespread 48V EQ Boost battery failures across the W223 S-Class (including 2022 S580) and other M256-equipped Mercedes models, with symptoms including no-start, stalling while driving, and disabled start-stop/boost functions. Battery replacement costs are commonly cited around $2,000-$3,000, matching the upper end of the listed range, but the safety implications (highway stalls, fire-risk ground connection recalls on sibling models) suggest the 'medium' severity rating is too low.

issues_found: Issue is real but largely describes normal EV charging behavior (taper, thermal management, preconditioning needs) rather than a defect

No NHTSA recall or specific TSB found for this exact issue on EQE; description conflates normal charging-curve behavior with a defect
audit.evidence: Owner forums (mbeqclub.com) document multiple EQE owners reporting inconsistent DC fast charging speeds well below the 170 kW spec, with battery temperature, preconditioning, and state-of-charge cited as primary factors. However, the more frequently cited M276-specific sensor issue is camshaft (not crankshaft) position sensor failure from oil intrusion into the connector, suggesting the entry may overstate this as an M276/M278-specific known issue.

issues_found: DTC codes P0730/P0777 are plausible but not the most commonly documented codes for 7G-Tronic harsh shifting; conductor plate-related codes (P2716, P0717, P0513) are more frequently cited

NHTSA complaints for Metris transmission are relatively limited - issue is more anecdotal/forum-based than dominant in NHTSA data
audit.evidence: The Metris uses the 722.9 7G-Tronic transmission, and harsh shifting/delayed engagement are well-documented issues on this transmission family, with owner forum reports specifically for Metris (e.g., 2-3 upshift jerks). results.title: Diesel Injector Leak and Black Death (OM651)

issues_found: DTC codes P0201-P0204 are generic 'injector circuit/open' electrical codes; Black Death (seal failure/carbon buildup) more typically presents as misfires (P0301-P0304) or no codes at all, with limp mode being a common symptom on OM651
Severity 'high' is likely overstated - this is a costly mechanical/reliability issue but not immediately safety-critical; 'medium' would be more accurate per the provided definitions
Year range is misleading for US market: GLK250 BlueTEC was only sold in the US from 2013-2015, not 2010-2015; the GLK220 CDI is a European-only variant
Cost estimate is on the low end - stuck/welded injectors and dealer-level repairs across all 4 cylinders can easily exceed $2000, especially when injectors are damaged during removal

Black Death is more historically associated with older OM611/612/646 engines; the OM651's documented injector issues are often faulty Delphi injectors causing limp mode, though seal-leak Black Death does occur on OM651 as well
audit.evidence: Multiple independent sources (Automotive Tech Info, idparts, Benzworld, intakecleaning.com.au, MBClub UK) confirm 'Black Death' is a real, well-documented Mercedes diesel injector seal failure causing carbon buildup around injectors, and it does affect OM651 engines as used in the GLK250 BlueTEC. However, the issue is most strongly associated with older OM611/612/646 engines, and OM651-specific complaints more commonly involve faulty Delphi injectors causing limp mode rather than the classic seal-leak Black Death pattern.

results.title: Power Tailgate Strut and Latch Failure

issues_found: Repair cost range may be slightly low - OEM motorized spindle drive struts alone can run $500-1000+, with full repair potentially exceeding $800
Description conflates two separate components - the system actually uses one motorized spindle drive (right) and one passive gas strut (left), not both being 'gas struts'
Latch failure is less commonly documented than strut failure - the primary documented issue is strut-related, not the electric latch

audit.evidence: Multiple owner forums (MBWorld X166, Go-Parts technical guide) confirm the GL-Class power liftgate commonly fails, with the right-side motorized spindle drive and left-side gas strut both being known failure points. The system is controlled by Tailgate Control Module N121/1 on W166/X166 platforms, and weak left gas struts often cause the motorized right strut to fail prematurely.

EQB-specific owner reports focus more on regen strength/adjustability and occasional 'solid pedal' moments rather than a clear 'dead zone' at low SOC

results.title: Timing Chain Variator Noise on M276/M278 Engines
